## Phase 0 after the 2026 re-assessment (binding context)

The original Phase 0 plan (a central 50 kt/yr processing station at Sun–Earth L4/L5, crew visits,
production LOX/LH₂, 100 kW-class freighters) was found not to close and is abandoned. Design for the
revised architecture below. Do not re-propose the abandoned design.

### Agreed by all three re-assessment models
- Split Phase 0 into 0A (research + pathfinders) and gated 0B (industrial): Structure agreed; budgets → §3 (All three)
- Abandon 50 kt/yr central SEL4/L5 ore processing: — (All three)
- Co-locate at least beneficiation and primary processing at the target NEA; ship product, not ore: Reference architecture (All three. GPT: "favoured but not universally optimal". Claude retains a central station fed with ≥20:1 concentrate as an alternative. Gemini's own weighted QOC scores SEL1 marginally higher (see §6).)
- Narrow product to native/reduced Fe-Ni; defer solar-grade Si and oxide-derived Al/Si: Fe-Ni baseline; Al/Si pilot or deferred (All three)
- Delivered product scale of order 1 kt/yr: 0.6–2.5 kt/yr (Claude 0.6–2.2 (central 1.3); Gemini 1.0–2.5 (1.5, of which 0.3 is water); GPT 0.6–1.0 contracted (0.67–1.33 capacity))
- MW-class cargo tugs: 1.0–2.5 MWe each; 10–18 tugs; 150–300 t payload (→ §3 for point values)
- Robots powered by HV tether from site power, with onboard battery for mobility and safe-mode: 1–3 kV; battery 10–50 kWh (Claude 2–3 kV, 10–30 kWh; Gemini 1–3 kV, 15–25 kWh; GPT 20–50 kWh, voltage unspecified)
- Delete the 200–500 MWh Li-ion line; size storage per site: 0.5–15 MWh total (Claude 0.5–3 MWh + thermal; GPT 1.3–3.3 MWh; Gemini <15 MWh (YAML 10 MWh))
- Reject $5/W array pricing: Hardware ~$30–150/W, launch separately accounted (Claude $30–150/W hardware ($50–230 installed incl. launch); Gemini $60–100/W (spec $75, range $50–110); GPT $30–100/W allowance ($45–220 with delivery))
- Replace 32–50 × 100 kg monoprop prospectors: Remote survey + 4–10 EP rendezvous scouts of 200–600 kg (All three agree a monoprop bus has ~0.5–0.8 km/s Δv. Remote-survey method differs (→ §3).)
- Add an Earth-to-space launch/delivery line: Line agreed; magnitude → §3 (All three)
- Add a comms, ground segment and mission-operations line; DSN not assumed free: Line agreed (All three. Claude and GPT reject the round-1 2.5 TB/day (~230 Mbps) figure.)
- Phase 0 uncrewed; remove habitat and quarterly visits: 0 crew visits (All three. Claude and GPT reject the "human-rating" label in favour of structural reserve plus docking/servicing interfaces. Gemini keeps docking ports and structural margins without commenting on the label.)
- Add an EP propellant supply line; xenon not baselined: Line agreed; demand → §3 (All three)

- Add NRE, pathfinder, spares and contingency lines: Lines agreed; values → §3 (All three)
- Write a full organization (bom-0-7) specification: ~$100–350M (Claude $100–300M; Gemini $150–250M (text $200M); GPT $150–350M)
- Add a debris/contamination requirement and budget tighter than 99%: $50–300M (Threshold → §3)
- Freeze one configuration-controlled baseline; mark legacy documents superseded: — (All three)
- Earth-supplied material as a fallback if microgravity metallurgy fails: — (All three. Ranking relative to lunar → §3.)
- Tie Phase 0 output to Phase 1 demand with a material/purity/date specification: — (All three)
- Add waste-heat rejection (radiators) explicitly: Item agreed; sizing → §3 (All three)

### Owner decisions
- D-01 (accepted 2026-10-12): Fund 0A. Hold 0B as a gated real option, sized at the gate by signed Phase 1 demand. Call Phase 0 a capability programme, not a cost saving.
- D-02 (accepted 2026-10-12): Hybrid: NASA life-cycle gates with TRL/AD² for each critical technology, plus four discriminating gates (target, demand, economics, licence). Stringency follows reversibility.
- D-03 (proposed; treat as interim): Set an ALARP requirement with an interim design ceiling. The number itself goes to modelling, tests and the licensing state.
- D-04 (proposed; treat as interim): Use SEL1 as the reference case. Re-decide jointly with Phase 1 at the 0B gate.
- D-05 (proposed; treat as interim): Select no propellant yet. Cost iodine as the reference case and argon as the alternate, pending the supply audit and life tests. Water EP stays a desk study until a C-type target is confirmed.

Under D-02, KDP-0B (the one-way commitment to 0B production) needs every project-ending technology
at TRL 6 in a relevant environment with no waivers; internal 0A milestones need TRL 4–5.

## Model Specifications:

## Claude Opus 5.5

# bom-0-5 Site Power, Arrays and Storage (Phase 0B): Technical Proposal

**Status:** Proposal for configuration-control review. Numbers are planning values with stated bases. None is approved.
**Supersedes:** All round-1 and round-2 bom-0-5 material sized for the abandoned 50 kt/yr SEL4/L5 station. That includes the 60–100 MW nameplates, the 15–60 MW_th station heat rejection, and the 200–500 MWh battery bank. Those numbers do not apply to the revised architecture and should be marked superseded.

---

## 0. Summary

| Item | My recommendation |
|---|---|
| **Scope boundary** | Site power only: generation, HV distribution, storage and site power management at the target NEA. **Tug arrays are counted in bom-0-4**, built on a common array-wing product line shared with this item. |
| **Architecture** | Modular 200 kW Site Power Units (SPUs), sized by the target's spin state. **Class P** (polar, vertical tracking masts) is the baseline if the target passes a spin-state screen. **Class E** (two-axis tracking, day-only production) is the fallback. |
| **Site nameplate (BOL, 1 AU AM0)** | **Class P: 2.0 MW** (10 SPUs, N+1). **Class E: 3.8 MW** (19 SPUs, N+1). Envelope 1.2–8 MW across 0.6–2.5 kt/yr. |
| **Delivered EOL power at design distance (1.3 AU)** | Class P ≈ 0.9 MW. Class E ≈ 1.8 MW. |
| **Distribution** | Bipolar **±1 kV DC** (2 kV pole-to-pole) trunk, spines and robot ports. Qualification target ±1.5 kV. Array strings ≤300 V, fully encapsulated. kV exists only inside insulation. |
| **Storage** | Survival and ride-through, not production. **Class P 1.0 MWh; Class E 2.1 MWh.** Envelope 0.6–4.5 MWh. Robot batteries are in bom-0-2. |
| **Delivered mass to NEA** | Class P ≈ 45 t; Class E ≈ 79 t (both including 15% system margin). |
| **0B recurring cost (this line)** | Class P **$0.28–0.78B** (central $0.50B). Class E **$0.47–1.33B** (central $0.86B). Planning P50 **≈ $0.65B**. Excludes launch/transfer, NRE, spares and reserve, which sit in other lines. |
| **0A cost (this line)** | $10–25M: specification ownership, supplier RFIs, ICDs, long-lead options. All development is in bom-0-11; the pathfinder kit is in bom-0-12. |
| **Gate-critical technology** | Anchoring in cohesionless rubble (inside T15) is the item most likely to end the project. Relevant-environment TRL 6 requires a subscale SPU anchored and operated on an NEA by the bom-0-12 pathfinder. |

---

## 1. Design philosophy

1. **Size to signed demand, in 200 kW quanta.** The site nameplate is an output of three things: the bom-0-3 energy balance, the target spin state, and heliocentric distance. It is not an input. The SPU is the procurement unit, so the 0B gate buys N units and nothing more.
2. **Put the arrays where the sun is continuous.** Small asteroids have very large horizon dip. A 15 m mast near the spin pole of a 0.5 km body sees about 14° below the local horizontal. YORP evolution drives many small-NEA obliquities toward 0°/180°: Bennu ≈ 178°, Ryugu ≈ 172°, Itokawa ≈ 178°. A polar mast site therefore gets near-continuous sun on a large fraction of plausible targets. That halves array size and cuts storage by about half.
3. **Storage is for survival, never for production.** No production process may depend on stored energy. Every bom-0-3 process unit must tolerate an uncommanded cold shutdown. Fe-Ni melt freezing in a crucible is a scheduling loss, not a hardware loss. This is the key difference from the abandoned MRE design, where keep-alive drove storage.
4. **kV inside insulation only.** High voltage is needed to make robot tethers and spines light. It must never be exposed to the charged dust, terminator plasma and vented process gas near a small body.
5. **No exotic power in Phase 0.** Beaming, fission and free-flying tethered platforms are rejected (§3.4). Solar-thermal process heat is a bom-0-3 trade I recommend they run (§3.5).
6. **Site follows tug on cell technology.** Tug arrays (10–45 MW across the fleet) dominate total array demand. The site (1–8 MW) rides the same wing product and qualification. bom-0-5 does not run a separate cell programme.
7. **Autonomy sized to the light-time and pass schedule.** The site must protect itself in microseconds, stabilise in milliseconds, dispatch in minutes, and survive 72 h without contact (30 days in safe mode).

---

## 2. Scope, boundaries and the tug-array decision

### 2.1 In scope (bom-0-5)

- SPUs: wings, masts, drives, anchors, string-level MPPT and DC/DC up-conversion.
- Power Management Hub (PMH): switchgear, solid-state circuit breakers (SSCBs), the site power management controller (SPMC), secondary buses, hub storage and hub radiators.
- Power spines (trunk cables) and Power Distribution Nodes (PDNs) with robot tether ports.
- Distributed storage: hub, plant UPS and PDN buffers.
- Seed Power Kit (self-deploying first increment).
- Installation tooling and end-effectors used by bom-0-2 robots to install power hardware.
- Site-level power FDIR software.
- Power-hardware contamination tolerance (dust, iodine, Ni-carbonyl) within the limits set by bom-0-15.

### 2.2 Out of scope (owner shown)

| Excluded | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Tug solar arrays | bom-0-4 | Common wing product; see §2.3 |
| Robot tethers, reels, onboard 10–50 kWh batteries | bom-0-2 | bom-0-5 supplies ports and protection only |
| Process radiators, thermal storage, furnaces | bom-0-3 | bom-0-5 radiates only its own PMAD and battery losses |
| Water pilot power | bom-0-6 load; SPUs supplied here as a **priced option** (§8.4) | C-type target only |
| SEL1 receiving-node power | bom-0-13 | May reuse the SPU wing |
| Array/PMAD/battery development and qualification | bom-0-11 | Requirements in §7 |
| Pathfinder power kit | bom-0-12 | Requirements in §7.3 |
| Launch to space; transfer to the NEA | bom-0-8; bom-0-4 / bom-0-16 | Mass and volume given in §5 |
| Orbital spares beyond N+1 in place | bom-0-14 | Recommendation in §8.5 |
| Reserve | bom-0-17 | No reserve is embedded in my cost figures |

### 2.3 Tug arrays: counted with the tugs

**Decision: tug arrays are counted in bom-0-4.** The reasons:

- A tug array is an integral part of the propulsion system. Its mass drives the trajectory, its PMAD is coupled to the thrusters, and its qualification is for transit and thruster plume, not regolith and dust.
- Counting them here would make bom-0-5 a 15–50 MW line whose cost is dominated by hardware that never touches the site. That is what inflated the Gemini and GPT round-2 figures (§9).

**Coupling preserved:** one array-wing product line serves two customers. It has one cell and blanket qualification, under T02 in bom-0-11, and one supplier contract with call-off quantities. bom-0-5 holds a site-variant delta specification (dust, rotation-cycle count, low-sun-angle operation, vertical orientation). The site's 1–8 MW is 3–40% of the joint buy, which helps the volume price.

---

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1 Site power classes (selected by target spin state)

| Class | Applicability (screen at target gate) | Array mount | Illumination fraction | Production mode | Storage role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P (polar)**, baseline | Principal-axis rotator. Pole within ~15° of ecliptic normal. A polar or high-latitude (≥75°) pad with horizon clearance from a 15–25 m mast. | Vertical wings on a mast rotating once per body rotation (VSAT-derived) | 0.85–0.95 (terrain-shadow model required) | Near-continuous | Fault ride-through, safe mode |
| **E (equatorial/general)**, fallback | Any principal-axis rotator, P = 2.5–20 h | Two-axis gimbal on a 5–8 m mast | 0.45–0.55 | Daylight only | Night keep-alive and ride-through |
| **X** | Tumbling (non-principal-axis), P > 20 h, or no anchorable pad | — | — | **Fail the target gate** for this architecture | — |

I am recommending that **spin state become a formal criterion in the target discriminating gate (D-02)**. Choosing Class E instead of Class P costs roughly +$0.35B and +34 t (§5, §8). That is a better use of a gate criterion than most mineralogical second-order effects.

**Horizon-dip basis.** Dip ≈ √(2h/R). For R = 250 m and h = 15 m, dip ≈ 20°. For R = 500 m and h = 15 m, dip ≈ 14°. At the pole, solar elevation oscillates within ±(90° − obliquity′) over the orbit, where obliquity′ is the pole's angle from the ecliptic normal. A mast whose dip exceeds that amplitude, plus local relief, sees continuous sun. Terrain-resolved shadow modelling from the bom-0-1 shape model is mandatory before the Class P assignment is accepted.

### 3.2 Site layout (Class P)

```
                       ECLIPTIC-NORMAL (spin axis, ~pole)
                                  ^
         SPU ring on polar cap    |      (mast heights staggered 15/20/25 m
     radius ~40-90 m from pole    |       to limit mutual shadowing at low sun)
                                  |
           SPU-3  o        o SPU-4
                \            /
       SPU-2 o---\--[PMH]--/---o SPU-5        PMH = Power Management Hub
                  /  |  |  \                        (switchgear, SPMC, 0.8 MWh,
           SPU-1 o   |  |   o SPU-6                  radiators, plant feeders)
              SPU-10 o  |  o SPU-7
                 SPU-9 o o SPU-8
                     |      |
          plant feeders     |
      [PROCESSING PLANT bom-0-3]  (adjacent, <=150 m; owns its own radiators)
                     |
        ============ SPINE A (±1 kV, ~0.6-1 km) ===========> to mid-latitude mining field
        ============ SPINE B (±1 kV, ~0.6-1 km) ===========> to second mining field
                 |          |          |
               [PDN-A1]   [PDN-A2]   [PDN-A3]    each PDN: 4 tether ports x 25 kW,
                 :          :          :          SSCBs, 25 kWh buffer, fiber hub
              robot      robot      robot         robots on 300-500 m HV tethers
              tether     tether     tether        (tether/reel/battery = bom-0-2)
```

In Class P, robots in a mining field at low latitude, where it may be local night, still draw continuous power from the polar hub. Robot operations become nearly 24/7, which is worth as much as the array saving.

### 3.3 Electrical one-line

```
 SPU (x N+1)                             PMH                                LOADS
+-------------------------+       +-------------------------------+
| Wing A strings <=300 V  |       |  BUS SECTION 1   BUS SECTION 2 |
|   -> MPPT/DC-DC (x4) ---+--+    |  +1 kV ===+====TIE====+=== +1 kV|
| Wing B strings <=300 V  |  |    |  MID  ----|-----------|---- MID |--> Plant feeders (2x, SSCB)
|   -> MPPT/DC-DC (x4) ---+--+    |  -1 kV ===+===========+=== -1 kV|    up to 1.2 MW (P) / 2.2 MW (E)
| roll ring (2 kV, 250 A) |  +====|=> SSCB                  SSCB <=|--> Spine A -> PDN A1..A3
| azimuth drive, anchor   | feeder|                                |--> Spine B -> PDN B1..B3
+-------------------------+       |  Bidirectional DC/DC <-> Li-ion|
                                  |  strings (4 x 0.2 MWh, Class P)|
                                  |  Secondary: 120 V DC (avionics,|
                                  |   heaters), 28 V DC (comms)    |
                                  |  SPMC (dual-string, cross-strap)|
                                  +-------------------------------+
 Grounding: structure and chassis tied to bus MID through high-resistance ground (~100 kOhm),
 continuous insulation monitoring on each pole. No reliance on asteroid "ground"
 (regolith is an insulator).
```

**Why bipolar ±1 kV:**
- Pole-to-structure potential is held at 1 kV, half the pole-to-pole voltage.
- One pole fault leaves the system able to run at half power, with pole isolation.
- It matches the agreed 1–3 kV robot-tether envelope.
- Silicon-carbide (SiC) power devices must be heavily derated for single-event burnout. A ±1 kV bus allows 3.3 kV-rated devices at ≤50% stress, or series-stacked 1.2/1.7 kV devices. A unipolar 3 kV bus would need >6 kV-rated parts with no radiation-tolerant heritage.

**Why strings at ≤300 V:** exposed cell interconnects at kV potential, near a terminator where dust and charging are active, are the most likely arcing failure. The 300 V string limit uses flight-proven SEP-array practice. All interconnects are encapsulated (grouted or coverglass-overlapped).

### 3.4 Alternatives considered and rejected for baseline

| Alternative | Why rejected | What would reopen it |
|---|---|---|
| Orbital microwave or laser beaming to the surface | End-to-end link efficiency in space is undemonstrated. Pointing to a rotating body and the receiver (rectenna) on rubble are both unproven. It adds a second spacecraft type. | A demonstrated >35% DC-to-DC end-to-end link at >100 kW |
| Fission surface power | Phase 0 needs about 1–4 MW; 40 kWe-class units would mean 25–100 reactors. There are licensing and launch-approval burdens, and the D-03 ALARP licensing state is still open. | Phase 1 demand at the 10 MW-plus scale on a non-solar-friendly target |
| Free-flying array platform with power tether to the surface | The body rotates beneath the platform. A tether from a sunward hover point to a surface hub only works with the hub at the pole. In that case, mast arrays at the pole do the same job without station-keeping (~0.5–1 N continuous thrust, ~1 t/yr propellant) or tether-dynamics risk. | A Class X target with a high-value orebody |
| Tug-as-site-power (docked tug backfeeding) | Tugs carrying 1–2.5 MW wings cannot safely operate in contact or near-contact with the surface. Their duty is transit. | Not reopened for Phase 0 |
| Electrochemical storage for night production (Class E) | About 2× array plus 4–8 MWh for roughly 1.6× throughput. Better bought as Class P via target selection, or as more SPUs. | A demand gate that needs more product from a Class E target |

### 3.5 Solar-thermal process heat (recommended trade for bom-0-3, not baselined here)

Induction melting at 35–50% electrical-to-melt efficiency is about 40% of the site's electrical energy (§4). A concentrator furnace (mirror on an SPU-type mast, about 600–900 m² of concentrator for 300 kW_th at 1.3 AU) could remove 0.3–0.5 MW_e from the array requirement. That would be 3–4 fewer SPUs, saving $80–200M.

It belongs to bom-0-3 because the furnace owns it. I ask bom-0-3 to carry it as an 0A trade with a decision before PDR. If accepted, bom-0-5 supplies the mast and drive as a variant SPU structure.

---

## 4. Load basis and sizing

### 4.1 Planning energy balance

These are **placeholders until bom-0-3 publishes its mass and energy balance**. Basis: 1.3 kt/yr delivered (panel centre), 1.4 kt/yr produced, feed-to-product 8:1 (ordinary-chondrite-like metal content with ~70% recovery), giving 11.2 kt/yr feed.

| Excavation and haul (bom-0-2) | 0.04–0.08 kWh/kg feed × 8 | 0.3–0.6 | 0.40 |
| Comminution (bom-0-3) | 15–40 kWh/t feed × 8 (metal-bearing feed grinds poorly) | 0.12–0.32 | 0.20 |
| Magnetic and size separation | 3–8 kWh/t feed × 8 | 0.02–0.06 | 0.04 |
| Melt and consolidate, induction | Ideal ~0.33 kWh/kg (c_p 0.45–0.65 kJ/kg·K, 250→1,800 K, plus ~0.27 MJ/kg latent); 35–50% efficient | 0.7–1.2 | 0.90 |
| *Alternative: carbonyl (Mond) refining* | Gas handling, reactor heat, compression | *2–5* | *not central* |
| Forming, casting, packaging | — | 0.2–0.5 | 0.30 |

| **Process total** | | **1.6–3.5 (carbonyl: 3.5–7)** | **2.34** |

- Process energy: 2.34 kWh/kg × 1.4 Gg/yr = **3.3 GWh/yr**.
- House load, continuous: avionics, communications, PMAD standby, battery and plant survival heaters at 60 kW. Over 8,760 h that is **0.53 GWh/yr**.

### 4.2 Power build-up to nameplate

| Step | Class P | Class E | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Production hours per year | 6,040 | 3,150 | 8,760 × illumination (0.92 / 0.48) × availability 0.75 |
| Process running load | 0.55 MW | 1.05 MW | 3.3 GWh ÷ hours |
| + house load | 0.06 | 0.06 | |
| + night recharge | ~0 | 0.15 | 130 kW × 3 h night (P = 6 h) at 90% round trip |
| × PMAD/distribution losses (1.06) | 0.65 | 1.33 | |
| × process-uncertainty margin (1.25, until bom-0-3 publishes) | 0.81 | 1.66 | |
| ÷ array-side factor (pointing, shadow, dust) | 0.90 → **0.90 MW** | 0.92 → **1.80 MW** | EOL at array, 1.3 AU |
| × distance (1.3²) ÷ (EOL/BOL × thermal gain) | ×1.69 ÷ (0.85 × 1.04) | ×1.69 ÷ (0.85 × 1.04) | III-V; cooler cells at 1.3 AU gain ~4% |
| Required BOL @1 AU | **1.72 MW** | **3.44 MW** | |
| SPUs (200 kW each) + 1 redundant | 9 + 1 = **10 (2.0 MW)** | 18 + 1 = **19 (3.8 MW)** | |

**Design distance.** Full production is specified at 1.3 AU. The site must:
- throttle production to 30% of full load down to 1.7 AU;
- hold survival mode to 2.0 AU, where Class P provides ~0.4 MW EOL, more than enough for house load;
- tolerate 0.8 AU perihelion thermally, which sets wing temperature and MPPT voltage range.

Targets with aphelion beyond 2.0 AU require a specific assessment at the target gate.

### 4.3 Throughput and class envelope

| 0.6 kt/yr | Induction, central | 1.2 MW (6 SPUs) | 2.2 MW (11) |

| 2.5 kt/yr | Induction, central | 3.4 MW (17) | 6.4 MW (32) |
| 2.5 kt/yr | Carbonyl, high | 5.0 MW (25) | ~8 MW (40) |

**Overall envelope: 1.2–8 MW BOL @1 AU.** This is the number the 0B gate refines.

### 5.6 Cell technology position

- **Must-pass screen:** the joint (tug + site) buy must be supplied at the required rate (≥10–15 MW/yr through 0B) with a signed delivery schedule.

- **Result:** the trade is close for the site, and the tug answer will dominate. Silicon at very high volume exists in-house at large LEO constellation operators, but not as a merchant supply qualified for interplanetary radiation. That availability question is the real discriminator, and the RFI must settle it.

### 6.5 Data and communications

- **Housekeeping:** ~0.5 kbps per SPU; ~5 kbps hub. Total power telemetry about 10–20 kbps, summarised for downlink.
- **Event capture:** 10 kHz waveform capture buffered at each SSCB, downlinked on demand (~1–10 MB per event).

- **Bandwidth position:** consistent with rejecting the 230 Mbps round-1 figure. The power system needs under 1% of any plausible link.

### 6.6 Anchoring (the dominant technical risk)

**Evidence.** On Bennu, the OSIRIS-REx sampling head penetrated about 0.5 m with negligible resistance. Philae's harpoons failed to fire. Surface strength may therefore be close to zero.

**Loads.** A 2.3 t SPU weighs only ~0.2 N at 10⁻⁴ m/s² surface gravity. Any disturbance above that unseats it. Drive torques are under 5 N·m, but robot contact, deployment snap, thermal snap and outgassing are not small.

**Candidate concepts, all in the bom-0-11 0A trade:**
1. Boulder grip: a clamp or bolt onto a ≥3 m boulder.
2. Ballast-bag skirt: regolith-filled bags packed by robots around a broad base mat. This adds inertia, not weight.
3. Deep helical auger or "root" anchor where there is cohesion.
4. Distributed guy-line web to multiple anchor points.

**Requirement:** ≥200 N holding in any direction and ≥2 kN·m overturning, with a 2.0 factor of safety, demonstrated on the actual body by the pathfinder (§7.3).

## Gemini 3.1 Pro

# Technical Proposal: Site Power, Arrays, and Storage (bom-0-5)
**Phase 0 - Space Resource Processing (Post-2026 Re-assessment Baseline)**

## 1. Recommended Approach and Design Philosophy
The revised Phase 0 architecture eliminates the centralized 50 kt/yr SEL4/L5 processing station in favor of distributed, co-located beneficiation and primary processing at the target Near Earth Asteroid (NEA), scaled to ~1 kt/yr of native/reduced Fe-Ni product. 

Our design philosophy for **bom-0-5** shifts from a monolithic gigawatt-class array to a **Modular NEA Microgrid**. We baseline a highly autonomous, 3 kV High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) distribution architecture powered by deployable thin-film/III-V hybrid solar arrays. Bulk storage (previously 200-500 MWh) is completely eliminated; instead, we utilize distributed, tightly coupled battery buffers (2 MWh per site) strictly sized for process keep-alive, fault clearing, and limited eclipse ride-through.

## 2. Technical Specifications

*   **Total Power (0B):** 5.0 MW BOL (Beginning of Life) per NEA processing site. (Yields ~3.5 MW EOL at 1.3 AU).
*   **Specific Power:** 110 W/kg at the wing level (including deployment mechanisms).
*   **Total Array Mass:** ~45 metric tons per 5 MW site.

| Power-related 0A activity | Attributed allowance |
|---|---:|
| Ground R&D, qualification, full-scale critical articles, and controls validation | $120–280M |
| Pathfinder power payload and power-specific flight integration | $40–120M |
| **Total attributed 0A scope** | **$160–400M** |

These are allocations for programme planning, **not extra bom-0-5 charges**. They exclude launch and whole-spacecraft costs.

### 12.2 Phase 0B recurring hardware

**Reference: 8 MW PV and 2 MWh stationary storage.**

| Hardware scope | Basis | Cost range |
|---|---|---:|
| PV wings and integral deployment hardware | $30–150/W at 1 AU BOL | $240–1,200M |
| Additional anchoring and site deployment equipment | Target-dependent allowance | $20–60M |
| PMAD, conversion, and switchgear | Separate from PV-wing price | $40–100M |
| Cables and connection stations | Route-dependent allowance | $10–30M |
| Distributed storage | $50–140M/MWh installed battery assembly | $100–280M |
| External power-system thermal hardware | Preliminary allowance | $15–45M |
| Controls and instrumentation | Preliminary allowance | $10–30M |
| **Total recurring hardware** | Rounded | **$0.44–1.75B** |

A working reference estimate is approximately **$0.8B**, before delivery, separately funded development, replacements, and programme reserve.

Across the broader **6–10 MW / 1–3 MWh** configuration family, use roughly **$0.3–2.2B** as a preliminary hardware scenario envelope. Capacity and cost assumptions must remain correlated; that envelope is not a probability distribution.

Supplier quotations must explicitly state whether PMAD, deployment structures, or thermal equipment are included. The table assumes the PV price excludes site-wide PMAD and stationary storage.

### 12.3 Delivery exposure

At 110–185 t delivered, a screening transport allowance of **$3,000–10,000/kg to destination** implies approximately:

\[
\$0.33\text{–}1.85\ {\rm billion}
\]

This is an attributed exposure in **bom-0-8**, not an addition to the bom-0-5 hardware line. It is not a trajectory closure or quotation.

Do not add another delivery-propellant charge if the adopted transport quotation already includes it. Otherwise, the unpriced propellant obligation remains in bom-0-16.

### 12.4 Procurement strategy

Authorize:

1. Supplier and manufacturing-capacity studies.
2. Qualification and initial production tooling.
3. A small initial module batch after KDP-0B.
4. Remaining modules after successful site commissioning milestones.

Do not pre-buy the entire installation merely to obtain an assumed volume discount.

---

## 13. Risk assessment

| Risk | Consequence | Primary mitigation / gate |
|---|---|---|
| Illumination worse than assumed | Throughput collapse or excessive storage | Terrain-resolved annual illumination model before target selection |
| Anchoring or deployment failure | Loss of expensive array modules; debris | Relevant-environment demonstration; independent modules |
| HV arcing in plasma/dust | Bus outage, erosion, fire-like thermal damage | Segmentation, qualified insulation, fault-energy testing |
| Feed grade or recovery poorer than assumed | Excess mining energy per accepted kilogram | Integrated feed-to-product pilot and target rejection criteria |
| Process shutdown energy underestimated | Battery depletion or plant damage | Measured shutdown tests before final storage sizing |
| Supplier capacity insufficient | Schedule slip and cost escalation | Capacity audit and production-representative contracts |
| Array pointing excites structural dynamics | Reduced output, anchor overload | Coupled flexible-body/attitude model and flight validation |
| Battery internal failure | Loss of reserve or propagation | Geographical separation, isolation, containment |
| Dust accumulation and excavation ejecta | PV degradation and radiator damage | Stand-off distance, source control, contamination budget |
| Delivery mass grows | Transport cost and schedule failure | Packing, trajectory, and deployment closure before procurement |
| Autonomous load management fails | Unstable bus or reserve exhaustion | Hardware-in-the-loop fault campaigns; independent reserve protection |
| Demand changes | Stranded industrial capacity | Modular procurement tied to signed Phase 1 demand |

For debris and contamination, follow the interim **ALARP** approach. Do not invent a “safe” release fraction. Model credible deployment, excavation, cable, and array-fragment release mechanisms and establish acceptance limits with the licensing state.

---

## 14. Where this proposal disagrees with Round 2

### 14.1 Reject 35–100 MW site totals as the revised baseline

Those figures largely retain power demands from the abandoned high-throughput mixed-product architecture or aggregate site and tug requirements.

They do not follow from a one-site, order-1-kt/year native/reduced Fe-Ni capability programme.

**My reference is 8 MW at 1 AU BOL, delivering approximately 2.5 MW at 1.5 AU EOL in sunlight.** Larger systems require a demonstrated load and demand case.

### 14.2 Accept the smaller site scale, but clarify its rating

Claude’s revised 2.5–8 MW site range is directionally closest to this proposal. However, “site MW” is ambiguous unless it distinguishes:

- BOL/1 AU array rating;
- EOL output at target distance;
- delivered bus power;
- and annual energy after darkness.

This proposal makes those distinctions explicit.

### 14.3 Storage should stay near 1–3 MWh unless measured loads justify more

The 10–15 MWh proposals are not impossible, but they are not justified by the current reference operating policy. Full-power night production is deliberately excluded.

The 2 MWh reference is supported by a stated emergency budget, with target-specific verification still required.

### 14.4 Reject $5/W, but do not treat $30–150/W as proven

The supplied hardware allowance is suitable for scenario planning, not a procurement commitment. Heritage flight contracts also cannot be scaled mechanically into a definitive industrial price.

### 14.5 Do not carry obsolete process radiator quantities

Radiator sizing must follow the revised heat balance. Neither PV nameplate nor abandoned mixed-product plant power determines site radiator duty.

---

## 15. Open engineering questions

Before preliminary design review:

1. What is the target’s full-orbit illumination history at candidate deployment locations?
2. Is routine production at or beyond 1.5 AU required?
3. What recoverable metal grade and recovery efficiency are supported by samples?
4. What is the measured whole-site energy per accepted kilogram?
5. What shutdown sequence and residual thermal load does the actual Fe-Ni process require?
6. Can the essential site survive on 25 kW, including thermal control?
7. What anchor concept closes under deployment, solar-pressure, cable, and tracking loads?
8. What tracking arrangement remains practical through the target’s rotation?
9. What qualified battery chemistry best balances calendar life, containment, cold survival, and mass?
10. What 3 kV insulation and connector design survives the relevant plasma/dust environment?
11. What are the process-plant radiator duty and allowable placement?
12. Can suppliers meet both site and tug array demand without an unbudgeted production-line programme?
13. What delivered mass, packing volume, transfer time, and propellant consumption actually close?
14. What contamination and fragment-release limits will the licensing state approve?

## Final recommendation

**Develop a modular 8 MW-reference / 2 MWh NEA microgrid in 0A, but purchase industrial capacity only after the target, demand, economics, licence, and TRL gates close.**

The central design principle is simple: **use sunlight to make product, and storage to keep the site safe.** Do not spend launch mass and capital forcing an unproven first industrial site to behave like a continuously powered terrestrial factory.

# bom-0-5 Site Power, Arrays and Storage: Consensus Synthesis

## Key Specifications

- **The site is single-digit MW, and the 50 MW round-2 figure is rejected.** All three revised proposals size the NEA site well below the round-2 35–50 MW proposals:
  - Claude: 2.0 MW (Class P) or 3.8 MW (Class E) BOL at 1 AU, within a 1.2–8 MW envelope.
  - Gemini: 5.0 MW BOL, about 3.5 MW EOL at 1.3 AU.
  - GPT: 8 MW BOL at 1 AU (6–10 MW), 2.49 MW EOL at 1.5 AU.
  - Claude and GPT attribute the larger round-2 totals to the abandoned station's demands, or to tug arrays being counted in.
- **Tug arrays are excluded from bom-0-5.** Claude and GPT state this explicitly (tug arrays sit in bom-0-4). Gemini's 5 MW is a per-site figure with no tug content.
- **The 200–500 MWh bank is deleted, and storage is 1–2.5 MWh nameplate.**
  - Claude: 1.0 MWh (P) or 2.1 MWh (E).
  - Gemini: 2.5 MWh.
  - GPT: 2.0 MWh (four 0.5 MWh units).
  - Storage covers survival, controlled shutdown and fault ride-through, not production through darkness.
  - All three reject the 10–15 MWh round-2 figures as a baseline.
  - Chemistry is space-qualified Li-ion at 100–160 Wh/kg pack level (Claude 125, Gemini 160 NMC, GPT 100–160).
- **Arrays use a ROSA-type roll-out blanket and a ~30% III-V reference cell, with silicon as a qualified alternate.**
  - Claude: ≥29.5% triple-junction.
  - Gemini: IMM at ~30%.
  - GPT: favours III-V but keeps competition open.
  - Wing-level specific power is about 80–130 W/kg (Claude ~87 W/kg at SPU level, Gemini 110, GPT 80–130).
- **Wing hardware is priced near $70–75/W within the agreed $30–150/W envelope.** Claude uses a $75/W central value, Gemini $70/W and GPT $30–150/W. Launch and delivery are carried in bom-0-8 by all three.
- **The 0B recurring line lands at roughly $0.5–0.8B central.** Claude gives a P50 of about $0.65B, Gemini $530M (including $80M of NRE) and GPT about $0.8B. Each excludes delivery and contingency (bom-0-17).
- **Distribution is kV-class DC with SiC switching and fibre data.**
  - All three use a 2–3 kV DC primary bus with SiC solid-state protection.
  - All three step down to secondary buses, and Claude and Gemini specify 120 V DC.
  - Optical fibre runs in power cables and tethers for EMI-immune control.
  - Claude and GPT add two rules: no use of regolith as ground or return, and continuous insulation monitoring.
- **Radiator scope is split by owner.** bom-0-5 rejects only PMAD, converter and battery losses. Furnace and process heat belong to bom-0-3.
- **Microgrid autonomy follows tiered load-shedding.** The priority order is: survival, avionics and comms first; then thermal/plant hold; then robot tethers; then process loads. Protection runs locally with no ground-in-the-loop, and the site must ride through comms outages (Claude and GPT require 30 days of safe-mode records or operations).
- **Production distance is 1.3–1.5 AU, with throttling beyond.** Claude and Gemini design for 1.3 AU and GPT for 1.5 AU. Claude and GPT both specify curtailment toward 1.7–2.0 AU.

## Divergent Views

- **Site nameplate and delivered mass:**
  - Claude recommends 2.0 MW / about 45 t (Class P), or 3.8 MW / about 79 t (Class E), built from 200 kW Site Power Units with N+1 redundancy.
  - Gemini prefers 5.0 MW with about 45 t of array plus 15.6 t of battery.
  - GPT suggests 8 MW from 16 × 500 kW modules at 110–185 t.
  - The differences come mostly from the energy-per-kg basis: Claude uses 2.34 kWh/kg process plus house load, while GPT uses a 4.5–6.75 kWh/kg whole-site envelope. They also come from the illumination assumption and from mass allowances for anchoring and structure.
- **Bus voltage and topology:**
  - Claude recommends bipolar ±1 kV (2 kV pole-to-pole), qualified to ±1.5 kV, with array strings ≤300 V and encapsulated. The rationale is that it allows 3.3 kV SiC parts at ≤50% stress for single-event-burnout margin.
  - Gemini prefers a 3.0 kV DC bus exported directly to plant and robots, mitigated by conformal coating and plasma contactors if needed.
  - GPT suggests 3 kV DC as a ±1.5 kV bipolar reference, with two sectionalised buses and a protected tie.
- **Storage sizing basis and price:**
  - Claude recommends survival-only storage, conditional on every bom-0-3 unit being cold-shutdown tolerant. He uses 4 h × 130 kW (P) or 6 h of night keep-alive (E), at $40–120M/MWh.
  - Gemini prefers 2.5 MWh sized for 1 h of 2.5 MW furnace keep-alive to prevent melt freezing, at about $10M/MWh. That keep-alive figure is internally inconsistent with Gemini's own "10% of full load" hold estimate.
  - GPT suggests an explicit emergency budget of about 0.73 MWh (25 kW essential × 12 h plus shutdown and robot recovery). This closes on 2.0 MWh nameplate with one unit out, at $50–140M/MWh.
- **Illumination and array mounting strategy:**
  - Claude recommends a polar-mast "Class P" site with vertical tracking wings on 15–25 m masts, giving 0.85–0.95 illumination. He wants spin state made a formal target-gate criterion, worth about $0.35B and 34 t against Class E, and would fail tumbling targets.
  - Gemini prefers radially deployed wings around a central hub, with no spin-state treatment.
  - GPT suggests spatially separated articulated array fields with terrain-resolved illumination modelling, rejecting targets whose geometry fails rather than proposing a polar layout.
- **Phase 0A pathfinder and cost attribution:**
  - Claude recommends $10–25M in this line. Separately, a 4–6 t, ~50 kW subscale SPU kit (1 SPU-P, mini-hub with 100 kWh, 1 PDN with tethered robot) would fly on the target NEA via bom-0-12 ($60–150M). It must anchor and operate for ≥6 months, and Claude treats this as mandatory for TRL 6.
  - Gemini prefers a 100 kW pathfinder at SEL1 or a proxy NEA, with $152M (including $120M NRE) carried in this line.
  - GPT suggests a 100–250 kW demonstrator, preferably on the target body, with $160–400M attributed to bom-0-11 and bom-0-12 rather than bom-0-5.
- **Power-system heat rejection:**
  - Claude recommends about 120–170 m² of two-sided radiator at 320 K (60–120 kW of hub losses).
  - Gemini prefers 1.5 MWth on an ammonia loop with about 1,500 m².
  - GPT suggests 110–220 kW of duty with about 700 m² reference area at 300–330 K.

## Open Questions

1. **What is the actual process energy per kg of accepted Fe-Ni?** Estimates span 1.6–3.5 kWh/kg for induction (Claude), 3.5–7 kWh/kg if carbonyl refining is used, and 4.5–6.75 kWh/kg whole-site (GPT). The answer is driven by native-metal grade and recovery: 20% versus 2% grade changes feed mass tenfold. It sets the module count and must come from the bom-0-3 mass and energy balance before PDR.
2. **What shutdown and thermal-hold energy does the plant need?** Specifically: can every bom-0-3 unit tolerate an uncommanded cold shutdown, and what residual hold load does the Fe-Ni process need? The answer moves storage from about 1 MWh to several MWh (Claude Q5, Gemini thermal hold, GPT's 25 kW essential-load question).
3. **Can arrays be anchored and tracked on rubble?** The concern is anchoring and tracking stability in cohesionless, ~10⁻⁴ m/s² regolith, given Philae's failed harpoons and Bennu's negligible surface resistance. All three see this as the likely project-ending T15 issue, and none believes ground analogues alone can reach TRL 6.
4. **Do kV interfaces survive dust and plasma?** This covers kV insulation, dust-tolerant blind-mate connectors and cable behaviour in charged dust and terminator plasma, with plant vents and EP plume (iodine) deposition added. It also includes whether 3 kV, rather than ±1 kV, is worth the arcing risk (T09).
5. **What is the target's illumination history and spin state?** The needs are a full-orbit illumination record, spin state, pole orientation and terrain shadowing at candidate pads, plus an allowable aphelion. This determines the array class and storage, and must be settled before the target gate.
6. **Can the array supply chain deliver both customers?** Suppliers would need to provide the combined tug and site demand (roughly 10–15 MW/yr) with qualified interplanetary radiation data. A related question is whether silicon is a real merchant alternative. This needs an RFI by the 0A mid-term.

## Recommended Approach

1. **Fix the boundary.** Tug arrays go in bom-0-4. bom-0-5 keeps a site-variant delta specification on a single shared wing product line covering cell, blanket, qualification and supplier contract. Record this in the configuration-controlled boundary table, along with robot tethers and batteries (bom-0-2) and process radiators (bom-0-3).
2. **Size in modules from demand, and report four ratings.** Procure standard 200–500 kW units whose count is set by the bom-0-3 energy balance, target spin state and heliocentric distance. Carry a planning envelope of 2–8 MW BOL at 1 AU, with about 4 MW as the interim interface-control value for 1.3 kt/yr. Always quote four values together:
   - BOL at 1 AU;
   - EOL at design distance;
   - delivered bus power;
   - annual energy after darkness.
3. **Make illumination a target-gate criterion.** Add spin state, pole orientation and terrain-resolved shadowing to the D-02 target gate. Adopt Claude's polar-mast Class P where the target allows it, Class E as the fallback, and reject tumbling or unanchorable targets rather than buying storage to compensate.
4. **Baseline a bipolar DC bus.** Use ±1 kV (2 kV pole-to-pole) as the operating baseline and qualify insulation at ±1.5 kV, so that 3 kV stays open for a 0A TRL-5 trade on plasma and dust margins and SiC single-event-burnout data. Keep exposed strings ≤300 V and encapsulated. Put SSCBs on every feeder, use two sectionalised buses, monitor insulation continuously, and never use regolith as a return path.
5. **Size storage for survival only.**
   - Use 1–2.5 MWh nameplate, about 2 MWh as the interim value, split into ≥4 geographically separated strings plus small PDN buffers.
   - Size it with GPT's explicit emergency-budget method, closed with one string out.
   - Make cold-shutdown tolerance a binding bom-0-3 requirement.
   - Price at $40–140M/MWh. Reject Gemini's $10M/MWh as inconsistent with space-qualified packs.
6. **Require a relevant-environment demonstration on the target NEA.** Place the requirement on bom-0-12: a subscale (50–250 kW) site-power kit, preferably on the 0B target body. It must anchor, track, operate a PDN and a tethered robot, and log ≥6 months or ≥1,000 rotations. Without it, T15 and T09 cannot reach TRL 6 without waivers at KDP-0B. Keep bom-0-5's own 0A line small (about $10–25M) and carry NRE in bom-0-11.
7. **Separate wing pricing from system pricing.** Use $30–150/W for wings only. Plan the installed site system at about $150–400/W, because masts, anchors, PMAD, storage and distribution are 50–60% of cost. Set a 0B P50 of about $0.6–0.8B against a scenario range of $0.3–1.8B.
   - Size power-system radiators from actual losses, about 100–220 kW and 150–700 m². Treat Gemini's 1.5 MWth as inconsistent with a 5 MW site's ~3% PMAD loss.
   - Release modules incrementally after KDP-0B, tied to signed Phase 1 demand.
